title: Kunti in the stands
hookLine: at the princes' tournament a stranger walks into the arena and matches Arjuna, and one woman in the stands knows him
carry: the wise see one self in everyone
tomorrow: who is Karna's father? the arena wants to know.
last: DANA: GIVING, EVEN WHEN IT COSTS.

lines: A DAY TO SHOW THEIR SKILL.
cards: Yesterday's scene came from further down the road; today we're back in the order of events, and Karna still wears his armor. A great arena in Hastinapura.
Drona, the princes' teacher, has arranged a day for them to show the city what they've learned. The stands are packed, Kunti among the women.
The cousins ride and fight and shoot, and Arjuna outshines them all, the text says, while the crowd roars. Then a sound at the gate. Someone new walks in.

teach.b: It's Karna, tall and shining, in his armor and earrings. He barely bows to the teachers. He turns to Arjuna and says, in effect: everything you've done, I'll do.
And he does, one feat after another, while the crowd stares. Duryodhana is overjoyed. Here at last is someone to match the cousin he resents, and he embraces Karna like a friend.
Then Karna asks to fight Arjuna, one against one. And now the story swings up into the stands.
Kunti sees the armor and the earrings, and she knows. This is her son, the boy she set on the river, about to fight another of her sons. The text says she faints.
Vidura has her revived with cool water and sandal paste, and she comes to and watches, unable to say a word.
Everyone else in the stands sees two rivals. One person sees two brothers, and she can't tell anyone. Hindu teaching takes that view a step further.

teach.h: THE GITA: ONE SELF IN ALL.
teach.b: In the Bhagavad Gita, spoken in this same epic, on the field where these two will finally meet, Krishna says the wise see with an equal eye: they see the one Self, the atman, in every being, and every being in that Self.

teach.h: THE WISE SEE ONE SELF IN EVERYONE.
teach.b: Rivals, strangers, enemies: underneath, one Self. Many teachers read Kunti's view from the stands as a small picture of that wisdom. The crowd sees sides.
The mother sees family. And the Gita says that, seen truly, everyone in that arena is.

how: The tournament scene, with Karna's entrance and Kunti's fainting, is retold by Mahabharata storytellers and on stage, where it lets the audience see what the characters can't.

o: a son his mother sees in the arena and can't claim
a warrior who refuses to fight his own brother
a prince who is banished after losing in the arena

p: the wise see one Self in all

s: Kunti recognized Karna by his armor and earrings
she knew him, fainted, and was revived by Vidura.
Karna knew Arjuna was his brother
only Kunti knew. Karna and Arjuna saw only a rival.
in the Gita, the wise see friends and enemies as different selves

games.q: the school hype account calls the other team 'the enemy' before the big game. by today's teaching, what fits?
o: play hard, and remember the same Self is in them too.
they really are the enemy until the final whistle.
don't play; competing goes against Hindu teaching.
games.why: Karna and Arjuna competed with everything they had. the Gita's wise see one Self in every being, rival included.

practice: Bring to mind someone you're up against right now: a rival at school or work, someone on the other side of an argument. Picture their face.
If you pray, join your hands and bow to them in your mind, the way Hindus greet each other with namaste. If you don't, just say quietly: the same Self, there too. Notice whether the face changes.

wordCard.voice: Karna's abandonment. A stranger matches Arjuna in the arena, and in the stands, the mother who set him adrift knows him, and keeps silent.

orig.note: Sanskrit ātman: the Self; the Gita says the wise see it in every being.

carryVoice: Your line: the wise see one self in everyone. Two rivals, two brothers, one Self. Tomorrow: who is Karna's father? The arena wants to know.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva (the exhibition of the princes' skill; Karna's entrance; Kunti recognizes him and faints; Vidura has her revived)
